organism.overview: Ornithorhynchus anatinus is a semi-aquatic monotreme; adult males deliver venom with a hind-ankle spur, making it a distinctive reference organism for venomous mammals.
naturalHistory: It is endemic to eastern Australia and Tasmania and depends on freshwater systems.
It forages for aquatic invertebrates using pressure-sensitive and electro-sensitive receptors in the bill.
Functional venom spurs are associated with adult males and become more active around the breeding season.

deliveryMechanism.summary: An adult male can drive a hind-ankle spur connected by a duct to a venom gland into tissue.
sequence: The hind limb is positioned against the target.
The keratinous ankle spur penetrates tissue.
Venom travels from the crural gland through the connecting duct.
Venom is delivered into the puncture wound.

habitats.name: Rivers, streams, and freshwater bodies
habitats.summary: Freshwater systems with suitable banks for burrows and benthic invertebrate prey.

ecologicalRoles.summary: Male venom production is seasonal and is associated with competition during the breeding period.

summaryPoints: Platypus venom is delivered by the hind limb rather than the mouth, distinguishing it from mammalian biting defenses.
Human envenomation can produce severe and prolonged pain, but this starter profile does not yet publish a full clinical pathway.
